_comment: IAM permissions policy — agrisync-raw-replication-role.
spec: FINAL_SERVER_AUTHORITATIVE_EXECUTION_PLAN (raw-bucket-backup-recovery)
AUTHORED, NOT APPLIED.
Scoped to exactly the two buckets in this replication pair, in exactly
the directions replication needs: READ + ACL-read on the SOURCE (to see
what to copy), WRITE + tag-replicate + Object-Lock-metadata-replicate on
the DESTINATION (to write the copy and preserve its lock state).
DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: s3:ReplicateDelete. Do not grant it. Without it,
a delete (soft, via marker) on the source is NOT propagated to the
backup — a delete marker created on the source (whether legitimate
cleanup or a mistake) leaves the object intact on the backup copy.
This is the point of the backup: it must not mirror deletes. A genuine,
founder-approved DPDP erasure that must also remove data from the
backup is a separate, deliberate, logged action — see the runbook's
'Erasure reaching the backup copy' section — not something replication
does automatically.
APPLY (founder only):
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name agrisync-raw-replication-role \
--policy-name agrisync-raw-replication-permissions \
--policy-document file://replication-role-permissions-policy.json
